question.text: The Consumer Price Index (CPI) measures inflation at which level?

explanation.text: The Logic: Per page 95, CPI measures inflation at the retail level based on prices paid by consumers, while WPI measures inflation at the wholesale level. The Trap: WPI is wholesale, CPI is retail/consumer. The two indices use different baskets and weightings, so they need not move in lockstep. Note: The CPI vs WPI definitional distinction is grounded in page 95. Any specific RBI inflation target percentages should be verified from an official source before being cited.
